title: The Atlanta Porch
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Landscape 3:2 warm painterly graphic-novel illustration for a theatrical autobiographical memory of Atlanta, Georgia. An illustrative imagined reconstruction, not portraits of known real people. A modest lived-in wooden front porch on a leafy Atlanta residential street at early evening, full of five adult friends of mixed ages sharing a relaxed, affectionate, lively conversation after working together. Four friends are African American, with varied brown and dark skin, natural varied hair and everyday casual clothing; the fifth is a light-skinned adult man with dark curly hair in an ordinary soft shirt, seated as one equal member of the group. Three men and two women, every person an individual with expressive face, unposed informal body language, someone laughing while another listens and someone gestures in a friendly disagreement. A small table with cups, a plain notebook, a grocery bag and a few ordinary tools suggests shared work and ordinary life. No money display, no stereotypes, no luxury styling, no war imagery. Some worn porch chairs drawn close enough that the porch feels almost full. A clear empty chair just at the edge suggests someone remembering the gathering with love. Textured cinematic ink and CMYK painterly print matching a serious graphic novel, but warm soft amber porchlight and deep leafy cyan evening shadows, tender and specific, no sentimental halos, no moral slogan, no text, no captions, no logos, no watermark. The image should feel like the memory of people one misses, lively rather than solemn.
identity_note: Illustrative reconstruction of the author's supplied memory; not likenesses of the named friends.
